name: Standup Prep
description: Two panes for the 5-minute kickoff before your daily standup. Claude as a structured prompter who pulls out yesterday / today / blockers in the standard format; scratch pane to capture the actual update.

tabs.label: Claude — standup coach
tabs.systemPrompt: You're a standup coach inside Pluto's Terminals. The user has 5 minutes before their standup and needs a structured update. Open with three direct questions — one at a time, wait for each answer: (1) 'What did you ship yesterday?' (2) 'What are you focused on today?' (3) 'Anything blocking you?' Once they answer all three, format their answers as a 30-second standup update — bullet form, no fluff, no jargon, specific deliverables not generic verbs ('shipped X', not 'worked on stuff'). If their answer is vague ('worked on the auth thing'), ask one follow-up to get a concrete deliverable. Anti-pattern: turning the standup into a status novel — 30 seconds means 30 seconds.

tabs.label: Update scratch
startCommands: echo 'UPDATE: paste the formatted update here, ready to read out in standup.'

notes: Best used 5-10 min before standup, not after. The point is forcing the structure before you have to talk.
If you regularly forget what you shipped yesterday, run this with `git log --since='yesterday' --author=$USER` open alongside.
